claims.text: Incorporating approximately 2 vol% Y2O3 nanoparticles into a CoCrFeNi-based high-entropy alloy by mechanical alloying will produce a uniform nanoscale dispersion.
A uniform dispersion of Y2O3 nanoparticles will enhance high-temperature strength relative to a non-reinforced CoCrFeNi-based alloy.
A uniform dispersion of Y2O3 nanoparticles will enhance creep resistance relative to a non-reinforced CoCrFeNi-based alloy.
A uniform dispersion of Y2O3 nanoparticles will enhance oxidation resistance relative to a non-reinforced CoCrFeNi-based alloy.
Nanoscale Y2O3 particles will pin grain boundaries in the CoCrFeNi-based matrix.
Nanoscale Y2O3 particles will inhibit dislocation movement in the CoCrFeNi-based matrix.
Nanoscale Y2O3 particles will inhibit grain coarsening at elevated temperature.
Obstruction of grain-boundary migration by Y2O3 nanoparticles will mitigate elevated-temperature grain growth.
Obstruction of grain-boundary migration and dislocation motion by Y2O3 nanoparticles will mitigate creep deformation.
The Y2O3 nanoparticles will enhance oxidation resistance at elevated temperature.
At approximately 700°C in an oxidizing atmosphere, the Y2O3-reinforced alloy will have higher tensile strength than the unreinforced baseline.
At approximately 700°C in an oxidizing atmosphere, the Y2O3-reinforced alloy will have a lower creep rate than the unreinforced baseline.
At approximately 700°C in an oxidizing atmosphere, the Y2O3-reinforced alloy will show less oxidation than the unreinforced baseline.
The anticipated benefits are bounded to oxidizing conditions around 700°C.
Performance benefits at significantly lower temperatures or under non-oxidizing conditions have not been established.
The magnitude of improvement depends critically on achieving a consistently uniform nanoparticle dispersion.
Process scale-up and long-term stability under cyclic thermal conditions remain unvalidated.
